# ethereum-optimism/optimism Daily Update (Mar 4, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's development focused on refining error handling in the Kona derivation protocol, enhancing the `op-devstack`'s network interface for generic component access, and improving `op-node`'s follow source mode for better sync status handling. Several new issues were opened concerning L2ContractsManager, Glamsterdam gas pricing, and `op-supernode`'s L2 CL P2P connection.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

### Derivation Protocol Error Handling
A bug fix was implemented in the Kona derivation protocol to preserve the original error kind from the chain provider when loading blobs. This prevents all errors from being incorrectly categorized as `PipelineErrorKind::Temporary`, which is crucial for accurate error classification and pipeline behavior, especially during L1 reorgs. ([#19357](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19357))

### `op-devstack` Network Interface Refactoring
The `op-devstack` underwent a significant refactoring to introduce a generic component access system. This "Simplified Network Interface" design adds a `ComponentRegistry` interface, which aims to reduce interface bloat and facilitate the integration of new component types. ([#18876](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/18876))

### `op-node` Follow Source Mode Enhancements
Improvements were made to `op-node`'s follow source mode, specifically to ensure that `LocalSafeL2` is correctly copied when the node is following an upstream node's sync status. This change addresses how `FollowClient.GetFollowStatus()` handles `Safe` data, ensuring more robust synchronization. ([#19330](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19330))

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
- [#19394](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19394) chore(deps): bump @hono/node-server from 1.19.9 to 1.19.10 in /rust/docs
- [#19393](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19393) chore(deps): bump hono from 4.11.7 to 4.12.5 in /rust/docs
- [#19390](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19390) chore(op-acceptor): v3.10.1
- [#19388](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19388) feat: register zk proofs feature flag
- [#19387](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19387) fix(op-supernode): Fix race condition in virtual node Stop/Start lifecycle
- [#19386](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19386) fix(kona-engine): reset on SYNCING FCU response after EL sync completed
- [#19385](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19385) chore(contracts,deployer): remove OPCMv1 and make OPCMv2 the sole OPCM
- [#19384](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19384) fix(op-node): pipeline reset to handle EL restarts gracefully
- [#19383](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19383) chore(rust): reth/claude experiment

## CLOSED ISSUES

### Kona BlobSource Error Handling
The issue where `BlobSource` was wrapping all errors as `Temporary`, leading to a loss of `Reset` classification on L1 reorgs, has been closed. This was addressed by a fix that preserves the original error kind from the chain provider. ([#19354](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19354))

## NEW ISSUES

### L2ContractsManager Concerns
Two new issues were opened regarding the `L2ContractsManager`. One highlights the need to document the `no-storage-variables` convention to prevent collisions with `ProxyAdmin` slots due to `DELEGATECALL` execution ([#19391](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19391)). The other calls for a review of `L2ContractsManager` for error swallowing patterns that could leave the system in an inconsistent state if individual upgrades fail silently ([#19392](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19392)).

### Glamsterdam Gas Pricing Impacts
Several issues were raised concerning the upcoming Glamsterdam hardfork and its impact on gas pricing. This includes the need to increase `PreimageOracle.PRECOMPILE_CALL_RESERVED_GAS` to account for increased cold SSTORE costs ([#19380](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19380)), and updating `requiredGas` for the precompile oracle due to EIP-7904 ([#19381](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19381)). An investigation into the broader impacts of Glamsterdam gas pricing on precompile acceleration is also underway ([#19375](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19375)).

### `op-supernode` and Flashblocks Issues
A new issue reports a broken flashblock websocket endpoint, with users experiencing handshake failures ([#19382](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19382)). Additionally, an issue was opened to fix L2 CL P2P connection for light CLs in follow-mode within `op-supernode` ([#19379](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19379)), and to add a test with a light CL as a sequencing node in `op-acceptance-tests` ([#19389](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19389)).

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### Initial EL Sync UX and Correctness ([#17631](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/17631))
Discussion continues regarding the behavior of `op-node` when it finishes initial EL Sync, specifically how it marks the reached target as finalized even if the block is not actually finalized. Recent comments from @karlfloersch question if this bug is specific to light CL/interop or if it's present even without it, and how such edge cases are currently mitigated. @trianglesphere previously noted that this was the intended design behavior for EL sync, but acknowledged it could be considered a bug now. @axelKingsley suggested that Snap Sync should only follow the finalized L2 as a maximum target to prevent incorrect data. @sebastianst agreed that this is buggy behavior and proposed running derivation from a prior L1 block and then consolidation to verify alignment with the EL-synced unsafe chain.

### Set default respected game type to CANNON_KONA ([#18640](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/18640))
This issue, aiming to make `CANNON_KONA` the primary game type after Upgrade 18, has been moved back to "in progress" by @stevennevins, indicating upcoming changes related to a specific pull request ([#19272](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19272)).

### flashblocks WS endpoint Unexpected ([#19366](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19366))
Users are reporting 429 rate limit errors when connecting to the flashblocks WS endpoint. @unclezoro confirmed similar issues, indicating a broader problem with access or rate limiting.

### Investigate Glamsterdam gas pricing impacts on precompile acceleration ([#19375](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19375))
The discussion revolves around the significant increase in gas costs for precompiles due to Glamsterdam and how this might break proofs. @ajsutton provided links to internal documentation and noted that `requiredGas` needs to be bumped to match L1 costs, but precompile input lengths might not need adjustment. The impact of increased calldata costs when publishing large preimages and precompile inputs also needs consideration. This issue is closely related to [#19381](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19381).
